summary: Renewed US-Iran/Hormuz escalation has lifted oil, energy shares and long yields while pressuring broad equities. Prefer cash-generative energy plus grid, water, cooling and operating nuclear; demand more valuation support from long-duration/speculative equities.

holdings.read: Strongest fundamental anchor and tactically helped by the oil shock. Avoid adding aggressively into war-premium strength; prefer a pullback or proof that physical Hormuz disruption persists.
Quality and cash conversion remain intact. Add only when organic growth/regional contribution begins to reaccelerate.
FY26 validates the operating reset and record unbilled sales improve visibility, but leverage and higher rates still cap conviction.
Johor data-centre and power scarcity remain supportive, but capex, leverage and cash conversion matter more as rates rise.
Price deteriorated more than the verified GTA VI thesis. The November 19 catalyst remains intact, making the selloff more interesting if price stabilises.
The stock is strengthening into the Sep 3 Cybercab catalyst while fundamentals remain valuation-constrained. Better event momentum, worse entry quality.
